rationale:
ROUND 4 of 7ba5b8c4. Round 3 moved to 8 approve / 2 object (from 5/3 twice) -- guardian, diagnosis_guardian, compliance and render_guardian now approve. Three objections remain and ALL THREE ARE FIXED HERE RATHER THAN ARGUED WITH. NOTE unreadable:1 for the SECOND round running, and the missing seat is `editquality` both times; round 3's first attempt also HUNG at review_editquality for 2h34m. Flagged for bugs_open/119, not used as an excuse -- the two objecting seats were readable and their objections stand on their own.

(A) bug_historian (medium) IS RIGHT AND THIS IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. I added a prune floor for kind='doc' and left the code rows -- the older, larger, already-populated half of the same table, under the SAME `DELETE WHERE repo=$1 AND commit_sha IS DISTINCT FROM $2` -- with no floor at all. Its words: 'This plan had the context and the call site open in front of it and chose to gate only the new addition.' That is exactly what happened, and it is 016b s9's 'one call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix; the sibling stays heuristic' with me as the author. FIXED: the floor now guards the WHOLE prune, per kind. A run that yields under half the stored count for a kind does not delete that kind's rows -- code and doc alike. The collapse conditions bug_historian lists (moved directory, permissions, partial fetch, files_read toward 0) apply identically to Go files, and a partial repo fetch is not hypothetical: it is the same tarball the docs walk depends on.

(B) prior_art_librarian (medium) FOUND A REAL BLIND SPOT IN MY 'EXHAUSTIVE' SEARCH. My grep was anchored `^func [A-Za-z_]*(...)\(` which STRUCTURALLY CANNOT MATCH A METHOD WITH A RECEIVER -- `func (p *Parser) SplitSections(...)` -- and a stateful splitter is idiomatically exactly that shape. The search that justified building flattenMarkdown fresh had a hole where the most likely candidate would live. CLOSED TWO WAYS. Receiver-form grep: `grep -rnE '^func \([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]* \*?[A-Za-z0-9_]+\) [A-Za-z_]*([Cc]hunk|[Ss]plit|[Ss]ection|[Hh]eading|[Pp]arse|[Ee]xtract)' --include=*.go . | grep -v docs/ | grep -v _test.go` -> 15 hits, NONE a markdown/document splitter: orchestration internals (extractGroupInfo, parseResponseBody, extractSpawnData, extractWorkflowResult), page-section helpers (sourceResolver.sectionDescription), config/JSON/CSV parsers, DuckDuckGoProvider.parseHTMLResults (HTML search results, not markdown) and FirecrawlScrapingProvider.ExtractStructured (LLM extraction from a URL). And a second sweep through THE CODE INDEX ITSELF, which stores methods in receiver form: `SELECT path, symbol FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='method' AND (symbol ILIKE '%chunk%' OR '%split%' OR '%section%' OR '%heading%' OR '%markdown%')` -> all *Section* hits are discovery-check types' Name/Run methods. The conclusion is unchanged but the search now covers the shape it was missing.

(C) prior_art_librarian (low) -- pipeline ownership, now attached rather than asserted:
  SELECT type, is_active, COALESCE(is_snapshot,false), default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'index_symbols'->>'action',
         default_config->'workflow'->>'start_step'
    FROM agent_definitions WHERE type IN ('code-indexer','index-orchestrator')
     AND deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT COALESCE(is_snapshot,false);
  -> code-indexer       | t | f | index_code_symbols | request_analysis
  -> index-orchestrator | t | f | (null)             | spawn_indexer
  SELECT name, target_agent_type, interval_seconds, enabled FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name='code-index-refresh';
  -> code-index-refresh | index-orchestrator | 86400 | t
Both agents seeded and active, the step action is index_code_symbols, and the scheduled task targets the orchestrator that spawns it.

(D) debug_historian (low) raised the migration's RAISE-on-rerun for the SECOND time and noted it stood only 'accepted', not corrected. Raised twice is a signal, so it is CORRECTED: the guard now RAISE NOTICEs and skips the ALTER, so a rerun is a genuine 0-row no-op that COMMITs cleanly -- the documented needle-gate shape -- instead of aborting the transaction and looking like a hard failure.

plan.summary: ROUND 4. D11 layer 1b: index MARKDOWN sections from four durable prose sources into code_symbols, reusing layer 1's body column and content search. Round 4 extends the prune floor to EVERY kind (round 3 guarded only the new one, leaving the larger code half exposed to the identical collapse), closes a receiver-shaped blind spot in the prior-art search that structurally could not see methods, attaches the pipeline-ownership SQL, and makes the migration guard a true 0-row no-op.

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- the mechanical blocker. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. READERS enumerated for guardian (round 1, medium): no reader switches on kind; diagnose_code_lookup never selects it; scanCodeSymbolRows selects it into lookup_code_symbols' result map only. NUMBER MOVES -- 253 is highest today, but this workstream's last migration was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241 and 242 inside four hours. Re-read the max immediately before writing the file.

ROUND 2, answering debug_historian (medium): the needle-gate discipline wants verify AND rollback as separate files, and this constraint relaxation is what makes the Go writer's INSERTs possible at all -- so a bad flattenMarkdown run had no scripted recovery. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT TRIVIAL: the old CHECK cannot be restored while kind='doc' rows exist, so the rows must be deleted FIRST or the ALTER fails with a check-violation on existing data. Written as one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable.

ROUND 3, rewritten for bug_historian (medium): the round-2 guard fired only on a TOTAL of zero, and round 1's real defect was non-zero-but-wrong-source. Now: counts are tracked PER GLOB and returned; a glob matching ZERO FILES is a hard error (the plan's only fail-loud escalation, because a source contributing nothing is indistinguishable from a source that does not exist); and the scope/path-shape assertion runs HERE, every index, not only in a VERIFY a human runs once. NOT REUSING, with the search attached in the rationale: chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396) is a fixed-width window; extractProductSection (vet_med_price_scrape_action.go:650) is markdown- and heading-aware but TRUNCATES at a fixed end-marker list and returns one prefix with no spans; no markdown parser is a dependency (goldmark is go.sum-graph-only, absent from go.mod, imported nowhere). Suffix determinism, for guardian (low): the counter is a per-file map[string]int incremented during ONE top-to-bottom pass over the file's own lines, so the Nth occurrence gets the same suffix every run -- document order, never map iteration order.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. composeSymbolContent keeps the code BODY out for exactly this reason; markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only; the section text goes to body, which is what the content check now searches anyway.

ROUND 4, bug_historian (medium): the round-3 floor guarded kind='doc' ONLY, leaving the code rows -- older, larger, already populated -- under the same unguarded DELETE. That is the sibling-call-site pattern (016b s9, bugs_open/093) with me as the author, on a call site I had open. The floor is now PER KIND and covers BOTH: a kind whose row count this run is under half its stored count is not pruned, and the refusal is logged and returned. Collapse conditions (moved directory, permissions, partial tarball) apply identically to Go files. THE GLOBS ARE THE DESIGN and round 1 got one wrong: the register is register/*.md (110 entries), not the parent (28 superseded planning docs). Pipeline ownership attached in the rationale, not asserted.

A SUPPLEMENT, not a fix -- explicitly conceding editquality (low, edit 6): this file changes no behaviour and is not counted as covering any mechanism. It exists because 243's VERIFY caught a real defect in layer 1 that a reviewer had been asked to eyeball. Carries the 243 lesson forward: that file's EXPLAIN stayed pinned to the OLD predicate after the code changed, so it reported on a query nobody ran while presenting as coverage -- these assertions must be re-read whenever flattenMarkdown or the globs change.

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT, unchanged: content and content_hash must not gain section text, or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only; the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows. (2) EMBEDDING COST IS REAL AND NEW: ~1,749 rows each embed once on first index. Layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction; this one is not, and it is stated rather than buried. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: measured at 1 today. The suffix counter runs in document order over a single top-to-bottom pass, so it is stable across runs -- if a reviewer can show a path where it is not, the prune/upsert churns those rows every index. (4) SCOPE IS THE DESIGN AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG ONCE ALREADY: the register glob pointed at 28 superseded planning docs instead of 110 register entries. That is the failure mode in miniature -- a wrong glob poisons the corpus with exactly the stale-doc class the plan exists to keep out, while every counter reports success. The VERIFY's out-of-scope assertion and the register_sections check are the guards, and the Go comment marks the value load-bearing. (5) BLAST RADIUS OF THE CHECK CHANGE, now enumerated rather than assumed: no reader switches on kind; the only behavioural change is that a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k. (6) ROLLBACK ORDER: the old CHECK is validated against existing data, so kind='doc' rows must be deleted BEFORE the constraint is restored -- the sidecar does both in one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable. (7) DEPLOY: Go is inert until the image rolls, so the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break. Confirm against the RUNNING pod with a string this change creates plus one it deletes, never git and never the tag. (8) The freshness banner keys on the indexed COMMIT (108 defect A, live v1.0.1189), so a prose answer carries the same staleness qualifier a code answer does.
